subject: RSHE
unit: Choose and try a calm step
title: Choose and try a calm step
display_title: Choose and try a calm step
focus: Choose and try a calm step
calendar_note: Year A. Spring 1 Week 3, 18–22 January 2027. Wednesday 20 January 2027, P1. One 40-minute formative lesson for three to four learners. Spring 1 runs 4 January–12 February for six weeks; Week 6 is assessing. No clock time supplied.
source_adaptation: C66 outcome retained verbatim. Inherited identifying source programmes/resources in A64/D64/E64/F64 rendered generically. Three authored low-pressure classroom routines from the owner brief and familiar school-agreed versions, not clinical treatment protocols. A maximum thirty-second practice timer is not a breath-rate demand. Independence means actual routine use with retained card/model/usual aids and no adult next-step content cues after the general task cue. Pupil helpfulness report is separate from observed independence. No distress induction, personal trigger account or guarantee of calming.

sources.note: Exact B66 and C66 verified. Inherited A64 strand qualifier and D64–F64 identifying alignment/resource details rendered generically. Raw workbook not distributed. Owner supplies date, group, access and six-week calendar.
Accepted BUILD RSHE format, both editions, Shared_Resources, Level 2 aids, short chunks and private help. New row-66 routine lesson; portrait bank from Week 2 is not carried over.

Wednesday 20 January 2027 P1, 40 minutes, Year A, group three to four. Three authored familiar school-agreed routines, brief optional practice up to 30 seconds, keep card and own Did it help? choice. Card/model/usual aids remain for independence; adult next-step cues logged separately. Word bank/starter/visible model every task, 10–15-minute chunks and faithful scribing for choice/reflection only. No personal triggers or public questions. Generic private help and safeguarding route. Pause for Downloaded.

source_end_check: Observe actual use of one chosen routine with retained card/model/usual aids, without adult step prompts, or record prompted/unobserved practice honestly.
timing: 3 calm arrival; 4 words/choice; 4 breath model; 1 reset.
6 count/move teaching; 3 private hinge; 3 choose/plan; 1 reset.
9 private timed practice/check; 3 feedback; 3 private exit.
source_timing: No fixed lesson minutes in row 66; owner specifies 40 minutes and 10–15-minute chunks.

routes.Supported: Teach one short step at a time first. Keep word bank, sentence starter, visible model and routine card. Offer two routine choices if needed. Usual aid or exact scribe records choice/check; actual practice remains the learner’s. Record all adult step prompts faithfully.
routes.Independent: Keep the chosen routine card, bank, starter and visible model. After the general task cue, learner chooses, starts and uses the steps without adult step instructions. Usual sensory, physical, reading, timer or communication access remains. Record actual practice and their own help tick.
routes.Aspire: Keep all Level 2 aids. Use one chosen routine, then explain whether it helped or what to try next. More writing or trying all three is not required. Independence means no adult next-step cues, not removal of normal aids.

level_2_scaffolds_every_task.model: Story A picks the soft breath card.
Soft breath in; soft breath out. No hold.

level_2_scaffolds_every_task.bank: three, two, one, open, close, rest

Story A picks soft breath. Other safe cards can fit.

level_2_scaffolds_every_task.starter: My card is ... . Did it help? ... .
level_2_scaffolds_every_task.model: A tries with the card. The help tick is their own.
A can keep the card and ask for help next time.

colour_blind_safe: Written IN/OUT labels, arrow direction, numbered steps and words carry meaning; no colour-only cues.

strategies.label: slow breathing
steps: Sit or stand in a safe, comfy way.
Use IN for a soft breath in.
Use OUT for a soft breath out. Go at your own slow pace.
Stop if it does not feel good. Ask for help or change.
strategies.staff: Use a familiar school-agreed gentle routine at a comfortable personal pace. No forced deep breath, breath-holding, phase counts, prescribed rate or closed eyes. Visual IN/OUT is a cue, not a paced demand. If uncomfortable, stop/choose another option.

strategies.label: grounding count
steps: Look for three things you can see.
Notice two safe points of touch, like feet on the floor and a seat.
Notice one sound you can hear.
You can stop or pick a new card if this does not suit you.
strategies.staff: A short authored 3–2–1 notice-and-count activity, not a treatment protocol. Normal setting only, eyes open; no taste, smell, unfamiliar object or touching another person. Use usual sensory access. If an element does not suit the learner, choose another routine or an already agreed access adaptation; no requirement to tolerate uncomfortable sensations.

strategies.label: movement reset
steps: Sit in your usual safe way. Rest your hands where comfy.
Close them softly, with no tight grip. Let them rest.
You can stop or pick a new card if this does not suit you.
strategies.staff: Use a familiar agreed small movement, seated or supported in the usual safe position. No stretch/range target, squeezing, force or physical performance grade. Stop if uncomfortable. Usual physical/sensory adaptations remain; choose another routine if this movement does not suit.

scenes.title: A wait for a turn
scenes.text: A young person waits for a turn. They pick the soft breath card. They look at IN and OUT and try a soft breath.

scenes.title: A new short task
scenes.text: A young person will try a new short task. They pick look and count. They notice things in the room, safe touch and a sound.

scenes.title: A pause in drawing
scenes.text: A young person pauses in a drawing task. They pick the small hand move. They open and close their hands softly, then rest.

timer_rule: One quiet practice of up to 30 seconds, after the learner has chosen and set up. Stop earlier if needed; no race or requirement to fill the time. Adult operates a familiar quiet visual timer with no sudden alarm. Timer operation is normal access, not a prompt telling the next strategy step. Do not count breath phases with the timer.
practice_rule: Low-pressure practice only, with calm invented third-person scenes. Do not induce a big feeling, ask for a personal trigger, require distress to start, or make calming down a condition of success. Learner may pass, stop, switch or seek private help. A safe try can be recorded even if it did not feel helpful. Pupil feedback remains their own, not filled by an adult.
independence_rule: After teaching and a general task cue, observe the learner choose/start/use their selected routine with their card, visible model and usual aids, without adult step-by-step content prompts. Record what was actually seen and any prompts. A scribe may record a choice or reflection but cannot substitute for the learner using a routine. Choosing to stop or seek help is respected; do not invent completed practice or claim independence when adult step cues were needed.
observation_states: Used steps with card/usual aids and no adult step prompts
Used steps with adult step prompts
choice_card_rule: Each learner keeps a choose-your-strategy reference card with all three short names/steps, a choice space and an initially unticked Did it help? choice. Point/select a routine; adult can mark the chosen option faithfully. Keep in the book or usual accessible place. No personal trigger or current-feeling question.
help_route: Point to HELP, write or ask to talk in private with a trusted adult through the school’s help route. If one adult is busy, use the route to another. Pass, pause and supported return available.
disclosure_note: If a pupil discloses, listen calmly, reassure and pass the concern to the safeguarding lead through the school’s procedure. Do not probe or promise secrecy. Keep details out of this pack and shared evidence.
private_help_route: Point to HELP, write or ask to talk in private with a trusted adult through the school’s help route. If one adult is busy, use the route to another. Pass, pause and supported return available.
scribed_route: Exact scribe can record a selected card, own helpfulness feedback or next step, read back and permit correction. It cannot perform the routine or turn a spoken/drawn explanation into evidence of actual use. Record observed action and any gap honestly; no health or breath-depth judgement.
worked_example_and_fade: Use invented A: chosen soft breath, IN then OUT at own pace, no hold. Keep step card and model visible. Teach/rehearse with adult prompts first if needed, recording that as teaching/support. For the later observed try give a general task cue and fade content prompts only; do not remove routine card, reading/sensory/physical aids or quiet timer access.
prompt_ladder: 1 Point to place/instruction. 2 Ask a short question privately. 3 Rephrase. 4 Offer scaffold/choice. 5 Model first step only, then return task. Allow processing. These content prompts support learning, but actual next-step prompts during practice must be logged and prevent an unsupported independent-use claim. Normal access remains separate.
adaptations: Cognition and Learning: four short routine steps, visible cue, one chosen option and reduced repetition. Communication and Interaction: wait time, familiar aid, pointing/selected feedback, exact scribe/readback. SEMH: calm stories, private choice, pass/stop/switch and supported return. Sensory and Physical: usual safe position and existing aids/adaptations; avoid uncomfortable sensation/movement, choose another card if needed. EAL: plan in any language. Colour is not the sole cue.
misconceptions: Independent means no card: correction keep normal aids, record next-step prompts. The timer sets breath rate: correction timer bounds an optional try only. Calming must work or get Yes: correction all four feedback options valid. An explanation proves actual use: correction observe chosen practice or record unobserved. Do not induce a big feeling or grade calm appearance.

main_hinge.claim: A card, visible model and usual aids may remain for independence; adult next-step cues are recorded separately.

parallel_hinge.claim: No or Not sure is valid pupil helpfulness feedback; it does not automatically mean failed independence.

success: Choose and use one familiar agreed routine with card/model/usual aids.
Observe whether adult next-step cues were needed, without inventing unobserved practice.
Keep own Did it help? choice and a next step; all four helpfulness reports are valid.

evidence.description: Actual selected routine and brief observed use, normal access and any adult step cues, separate own Did it help? report, kept choice card, one next step and reply. Faithful scribing records choice/report; it cannot substitute for actual routine use.

assessment: After teaching and a general task cue, observe the learner choose/start/use their selected routine with their card, visible model and usual aids, without adult step-by-step content prompts. Record what was actually seen and any prompts. A scribe may record a choice or reflection but cannot substitute for the learner using a routine. Choosing to stop or seek help is respected; do not invent completed practice or claim independence when adult step cues were needed.
where_this_leads: This helps me choose a safe routine, use agreed aids and say whether a step helped during learning or future work.

paragraphs_in_document_order: Teacher and cover planner
Choose and try a calm step
Wednesday 20 January 2027 · P1 · 40 minutes · Year A
BUILD · three to four learners · Spring 1 Week 3 · formative
Theme Resilience & Change. Six-week term; Week 6 assessing.
Thread tags: SMSC S/So (M/C none); British Values IL/MR (D/RL/T none).
Exact source outcome
Use a calming strategy independently.
Source: BUILD Weekly - Spring, PSHE & Citizenship, row 66. B66 Spr1·W3 and C66 exact. Named framework/resource context generic; no accreditation or therapeutic claim.
What this lesson teaches

Teach three short, school-agreed routines: soft breath, look and count, small hand move. Learner chooses one, tries the steps with usual access after a general cue, and gives their own Did it help? feedback. Independence means no adult next-step content prompts, not removal of a card or aids. A pass/stop/switch is respected and recorded honestly.
Prepare

Books, three routine cards, the single-page keep card in Support Cards page 4, vocabulary and staff evidence record. Adult-operated familiar quiet visual timer with no alarm, set only after choice/setup. Confirm safe usual positions, existing sensory/physical adaptations and private help. No distress induction or personal trigger questions. No new breath-rate/count protocol.
Source and calendar

Wednesday 20 January 2027 P1, Year A. Week range 18–22 January; six-week Spring 1, Week 6 assessing. Owner supplies timetable. C66 exact; identifying source resource labels generic. This is low-pressure practice, not treatment or a health assessment.
Where this leads
This helps me choose a safe routine, use agreed aids and say whether a step helped during learning or future work.
Forty minute sequence
Chunk
Minutes
Teaching
Chunk 1
3 calm arrival; 4 words/choice; 4 breath model; 1 reset.
Chunk 2
6 count/move teaching; 3 private hinge; 3 choose/plan; 1 reset.
Chunk 3
9 private timed practice/check; 3 feedback; 3 private exit.

Chunks last 12, 13 and 15 minutes. Two one-minute resets are included. Practice is one optional quiet try of up to 30 seconds, not a thirty-second breathing cycle. No race, minimum time or requirement to complete all routines. Reduce repetitions for access.
Chunk 1

0–3 calm starter: story A and choice of a card; no current-feeling question. 3–7 pre-teach card/help/stop, three choices, pass/stop/switch and own feedback. 7–11 teach soft breath one short step at a time with the IN/OUT image, exact written steps and visible model. Soft breath at comfortable personal pace; no hold or phase counts. Privately check IN/OUT; supported rehearsal is teaching, not independent evidence. 11–12 reset.
Chunk 2

12–18 teach look-and-count 3 see/2 safe contact points/1 sound, eyes open, and the small seated hand movement. Use normal environment and usual access; no touching another person, forced sensation or movement demand. 18–21 main hinge B: card/usual aids can stay without adult next-step cues; false A removes all aids. Parallel A: No/Not sure is valid own feedback, not failure. 21–24 choose/plan one routine with Level 2 bank/starter/model. 24–25 reset.
Chunk 3

25–34 private choice/setup, one quiet practice of up to 30 seconds and brief own check. General cue: choose a card and try its steps if you wish. Adult runs timer without giving the next content step. Observe actual chosen practice, access and prompts; no copied model or scribe can replace it. Stop earlier/pass/switch respected; missing practice stays unobserved. 34–37 one next step and response. 37–40 private exit and own Did it help? choice; keep the card in book/usual accessible place.
Scaffolds and response routes
Level 2 on every task

All seven tasks keep a short bank, starter and visible worked model: Starter, Model check, Guided count and move, Private hinge, Choose and plan, Timed practice and check, Feedback and exit. They appear on Support Cards pages 5–6. Independent work retains aids; the learner supplies the routine actions rather than adult next-step instructions.
Supported

Teach one short step at a time first. Keep word bank, sentence starter, visible model and routine card. Offer two routine choices if needed. Usual aid or exact scribe records choice/check; actual practice remains the learner’s. Record all adult step prompts faithfully.
Independent

Keep the chosen routine card, bank, starter and visible model. After the general task cue, learner chooses, starts and uses the steps without adult step instructions. Usual sensory, physical, reading, timer or communication access remains. Record actual practice and their own help tick.
Aspire

Keep all Level 2 aids. Use one chosen routine, then explain whether it helped or what to try next. More writing or trying all three is not required. Independence means no adult next-step cues, not removal of normal aids.
Worked example and fade

Use invented A: chosen soft breath, IN then OUT at own pace, no hold. Keep step card and model visible. Teach/rehearse with adult prompts first if needed, recording that as teaching/support. For the later observed try give a general task cue and fade content prompts only; do not remove routine card, reading/sensory/physical aids or quiet timer access.
Scribed route

Exact scribe can record a selected card, own helpfulness feedback or next step, read back and permit correction. It cannot perform the routine or turn a spoken/drawn explanation into evidence of actual use. Record observed action and any gap honestly; no health or breath-depth judgement.
Prompt ladder and TA focus

1 Point to place/instruction. 2 Ask a short question privately. 3 Rephrase. 4 Offer scaffold/choice. 5 Model first step only, then return task. Allow processing. These content prompts support learning, but actual next-step prompts during practice must be logged and prevent an unsupported independent-use claim. Normal access remains separate.
Book first

Routine cards are reference material. The dedicated page-4 keep card has a blank choice and four unticked Did it help? choices for the learner’s own mark/selection; keep in book/usual accessible place. This tick card is intentional. Other responses use book/usual aid. Plan in any language.
Checks access and private help
Check after the model

IN means a soft breath in; OUT a soft breath out. Own slow comfortable pace, no hold or timed breath phases. No forced deep breath. Learner can stop/change/seek help. Use bank/start/model and private pointing or aid.
Main and parallel hinge

Main B: the chosen card and usual aids may stay; adult does not give each next content step. False A says all aids must be removed. Parallel A: No or Not sure to Did it help? is valid feedback; false B treats it as failure. Re-model/recheck privately; a pass remains unobserved. A useful try need not produce Yes.
Planned adaptations

Cognition and Learning: four short routine steps, visible cue, one chosen option and reduced repetition. Communication and Interaction: wait time, familiar aid, pointing/selected feedback, exact scribe/readback. SEMH: calm stories, private choice, pass/stop/switch and supported return. Sensory and Physical: usual safe position and existing aids/adaptations; avoid uncomfortable sensation/movement, choose another card if needed. EAL: plan in any language. Colour is not the sole cue.
Private help route
Point to HELP, write or ask to talk in private with a trusted adult through the school’s help route. If one adult is busy, use the route to another. Pass, pause and supported return available.
Staff response

If a pupil discloses, listen calmly, reassure and pass the concern to the safeguarding lead through the school’s procedure. Do not probe or promise secrecy. Keep details out of this pack and shared evidence.
Misconceptions

Independent means no card: correction keep normal aids, record next-step prompts. The timer sets breath rate: correction timer bounds an optional try only. Calming must work or get Yes: correction all four feedback options valid. An explanation proves actual use: correction observe chosen practice or record unobserved. Do not induce a big feeling or grade calm appearance.
Evidence and feedback
What to keep

Actual chosen routine, general cue, start/steps seen, duration/stop, usual access, adult content prompts and one of the three observation states. Keep learner’s own Did it help? response on the dedicated card, plus first try, NS/reply and follow-up. A scribe can preserve feedback but cannot substitute for action.
Judgement

After teaching and a general task cue, observe the learner choose/start/use their selected routine with their card, visible model and usual aids, without adult step-by-step content prompts. Record what was actually seen and any prompts. A scribe may record a choice or reflection but cannot substitute for the learner using a routine. Choosing to stop or seek help is respected; do not invent completed practice or claim independence when adult step cues were needed.

Three recording states: Used steps with card/usual aids and no adult step prompts; Used steps with adult step prompts; Practice not observed this time. Observe only what is visible/known; a card on the desk alone does not prove use. Do not monitor or grade breath depth/rate, bodily appearance or health. Earlier supported teaching and later observed use are recorded separately.
Feedback and marking

One next step might use the chosen card’s first step or ask for an agreed access change. Keep first try and reply separate. VF spoken feedback; WS with support; I own use without adult next-step cues; NS next step; // self-edit; ? read back; E actual saved evidence. R only after Voice, Audience, NS and response in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode.
Evidence record

Evidence Sheet page 1 is pupil guidance; page 2 private staff record with fourteen blank entry rows and exact disclosure note. Dedicated keep card is Support page 4, with choice/feedback initially blank. Adult may faithfully mark a choice or feedback given by learner, never fill it from an assumption. Offer to Communication portfolio; staff confirm mapping.
Continuity

Week 3 formative; Week 6 assessing. Builds on naming feelings/help by teaching and observing a chosen routine, without requiring distress. Existing school-agreed routines and access only; no treatment or guaranteed calming claim.
Scope
Only BUILD RSHE Spring 1 Week 3 authored. No later weeks or separate RSE content. Pause for Downloaded.

Staff answers and teaching notes
Outcome and boundaries
Use a calming strategy independently.

Low-pressure practice only, with calm invented third-person scenes. Do not induce a big feeling, ask for a personal trigger, require distress to start, or make calming down a condition of success. Learner may pass, stop, switch or seek private help. A safe try can be recorded even if it did not feel helpful. Pupil feedback remains their own, not filled by an adult.
Three routines
slow breathing

Use a familiar school-agreed gentle routine at a comfortable personal pace. No forced deep breath, breath-holding, phase counts, prescribed rate or closed eyes. Visual IN/OUT is a cue, not a paced demand. If uncomfortable, stop/choose another option.
grounding count

A short authored 3–2–1 notice-and-count activity, not a treatment protocol. Normal setting only, eyes open; no taste, smell, unfamiliar object or touching another person. Use usual sensory access. If an element does not suit the learner, choose another routine or an already agreed access adaptation; no requirement to tolerate uncomfortable sensations.
movement reset

Use a familiar agreed small movement, seated or supported in the usual safe position. No stretch/range target, squeezing, force or physical performance grade. Stop if uncomfortable. Usual physical/sensory adaptations remain; choose another routine if this movement does not suit.
Timer

One quiet practice of up to 30 seconds, after the learner has chosen and set up. Stop earlier if needed; no race or requirement to fill the time. Adult operates a familiar quiet visual timer with no sudden alarm. Timer operation is normal access, not a prompt telling the next strategy step. Do not count breath phases with the timer.
Model check

IN soft in, OUT soft out, own comfortable pace, no hold/rate/phase count. The visual labels cue an action; they do not prescribe timing. Stop/change/help options remain. Supported rehearsal is teaching, not evidence of later independent use.
Independent use and own feedback
Main and parallel hinge

Main B: chosen card, visible model and usual aids can stay while adult refrains from next-step content cues. False A removes all aids. Parallel A: No or Not sure is valid own Did it help? feedback; false B treats it as failure. Re-model and recheck privately; a pass unobserved.
Evidence of actual use

After teaching and a general task cue, observe the learner choose/start/use their selected routine with their card, visible model and usual aids, without adult step-by-step content prompts. Record what was actually seen and any prompts. A scribe may record a choice or reflection but cannot substitute for the learner using a routine. Choosing to stop or seek help is respected; do not invent completed practice or claim independence when adult step cues were needed.

Use the three exact recording states: Used steps with card/usual aids and no adult step prompts; Used steps with adult step prompts; Practice not observed this time. A visible card or scribed explanation does not prove actual practice. Record only actions actually observed/known, any next-step prompts and gaps. Do not infer breath depth, physiology, distress or health benefit from appearance.
Own feedback

Did it help? Yes, A bit, No and Not sure all valid. Do not fill the learner’s mark from the adult’s view, treat No as failure or require Yes for independent use. Choice/feedback may be pointed or faithfully scribed, while the routine itself remains the learner’s action.
Keep card

Each learner keeps a choose-your-strategy reference card with all three short names/steps, a choice space and an initially unticked Did it help? choice. Point/select a routine; adult can mark the chosen option faithfully. Keep in the book or usual accessible place. No personal trigger or current-feeling question.
Next step

Record one useful next step based on what happened: practise a step with support, choose another agreed routine, or agree an access change. Keep first try and reply distinct. Actual content prompting is logged, not hidden by an independent label.
